name: Amara
catalog_quote: The syllabic canon of Amara is: (C1) V (C2), where C1 can be any consonant, a sequence of any stop plus any resonant, or the sequence ks; where V stands for any vowel; and where C2 stands for any consonant. Primary stress occurs on the penultimate syllabic vowel.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation is verbatim on Thurston 1996:205 in the PDF we hold p.215, page image read), together with the stress-marked forms named in the domain locator. (2) Deciding source is a 1996 Pacific Linguistics grammar sketch by the sole fieldworker on the language; Glottolog has exactly one descriptive reference for amar1272 and it is this one; web search turned up no phonology paper, thesis, JIPA illustration or acoustic study. (3) The only other primary statement, Thurston 1987:34 (downloaded now to, says isolation-form stress is 'usually penultimate' in all NW New Britain languages including Amara — consistent with fixed-strict penultimate (penultimate stress). The 1996 formulation 'penultimate syllabic vowel' matters only for glide-final sequences ([nákai̯], [iponéi̯ki]) and does not change the syllable-count codi
